title: Palmetto Robotics - Portout feasibility & benchmark kickoff
summary: Initial discovery for port-out compatibility from OpenAI/TGI stack into Redwood hosted/dedicated/private. Focus on eval parity, vLLM/TGI runtime artifacts, on-prem constraints, encryption/KMS, and a first benchmark plan. Agreed to run a 2-week parity bench and share security docs and pricing sheet.
topics: Eval parity goals and metrics (latency/P95, token cost, hallucination rate)
Hosting options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
Benchmark plan: sample prompts, dataset, metrics, run cadence
action_items: Maya Patel - Share Redwood benchmark template + sample prompt set by 2026-09-06
Gus Romero - Prepare TGI/vLLM compatibility checklist and known deltas by 2026-09-08
Priya Rao - Provide sample inference traffic profile and 3 representative prompt families by 2026-09-07
Samira Kaur - Send list of compliance questions (SOC2/ISO) that need answering by 2026-09-06
next_steps: Run 2-week parity benchmark on Redwood hosted with the provided prompt set
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) to walk through vLLM artifact conversion — proposed 2026-09-10
Send security pack and pricing worksheet (Redwood) within 48 hours
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-04 15:00 PT
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Gus (Redwood SE), Anika (CSM), Oliver (CTO Palmetto), Priya (Head of MLOps), Ethan (Infra Lead), Samira (Security)

Auto-generated summary:
Maya: Thanks everyone for joining, really excited to learn about Palmetto's port-out considerations. They are evaluating moving the inference load off their current OpenAI + self-hosted vllm/TGI pipeline into Redwood. Key asks are parity on quality, predictable latency cost, and support for private/VPC deployments.

[00:00] Maya: All right, hey everyone this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Gus our senior SE, and Anika on the CSM side. Oliver, do you want to quick intro?
[00:18] Oliver: Yeah hi, Oliver Hwang, CTO at Palmetto Robotics. We've been running a hybrid stack — main generation calls to OpenAI for few-shot RAG plus some self-hosted v-l-l-m instances for on-prem tasks. We're investigating an escape from relying on multiple vendors, trying to consolidate.
[00:35] Priya: And I'm Priya, we run the ML infra team. Our biggest pain is inconsistent latency and opaque token costs. Also the model artefacts from TGI sometimes behave differently than OpenAI outputs.
[00:50] Maya: Great, that's exactly the sort of thing Redwood is built for. Quick question to ground things: are you looking hosted first or straight to a private/VPC on-prem?
[01:06] Ethan: We prefer hosted for quick parity runs, but long term Dedicated or Private for data residency. A lot depends on what the benchmark shows.
[01:20] Gus: Cool. Can you describe the vLLM/TGI pieces — are you running TGI forks, and which models are you serving in vllm?
[01:35] Priya: We're mostly on an in-house fork of TGI that wraps some Llama-2 and Mistral variants. We also have a vLLM deployment for low-latency local inference. There are some KV cache hacks we use which I'm not sure will translate.
[01:53] Gus: Right, KV cache workarounds can change startup latency. We'll note that for benchmarking. Also, we do compatibility mappings for load/store of key-value cache, but sometimes the TGI tokenization differences cause subtle output skew.
[02:09] Oliver: Exactly. We saw prompts that pass on OpenAI but the self-hosted model hallucinated more. Need to measure hallucination rate, also P95 latency, and token cost per 1M tokens.
[02:26] Maya: That sounds like a clear success criteria set — quality parity (measured via hallucination/regression tests), latency SLOs (P50/P95), and cost targets. We'll capture that.
[02:40] Samira: From security we need to see KMS support, HSM integrations, SSO/SAML, audit logs retention, and incident response playbook. Also data residency for EU customers.
[02:58] Anika: We have templates for that — will put the security pack in the shared drive.

[03:15] --- Topics: benchmark design ---
[03:20] Gus: For the benchmark we usually ask for: representative prompt set (2-3 families), expected concurrency/tps, sample context lengths, and eval metrics — do you have that?
[03:33] Priya: Yeah we'll provide three prompt families: control commands for robotics, troubleshooting diagnostic dialogues, and a customer-facing natural language generation use case. Concurrency peaks around 140 RPS right now with big spikes.
[03:48] Ethan: Peak 140 is bursty though, average is more like 20 rps. We can share a 7-day trace.
[03:58] Gus: Good, that helps sizing. We'll suggest a two-week parity run on Redwood hosted, then a Dedicated pilot to test reserved capacity behavior.
[04:12] Oliver: Any concerns about model weights and licensing when moving models into Redwood private? We have some third-party model licenses to consider.
[04:23] Maya: We'll need a quick license check. Private deployments can host customer-provided model files, but our legal can review. We'll also map which models we can serve hosted vs private.

[04:40] --- Random transcript noise / recognition errors (as often happens) ---
[04:44] Speaker 6: (off) yeah so the T G I thing, it's kinda like v-l-l-m wrapper right, um the tokenizer split's odd
[04:53] Gus: yeah tokenizer/tokenization differences — sometimes 'Mistral' gets mis-transcribed in notes as 'mitral' which is just the ASR doing its thing.

[05:10] Priya: On the cost side, our CFO cares about per-token unit economics. Right now OpenAI is opaque and the vLLM infra is heavy on GPU. If Redwood can show a lower effective cost per token with similar quality, that's the sell.
[05:28] Maya: We can run a cost-to-serve analysis post-benchmark. Redwood Optimize recommendations often reduce unit cost via batching and KV reuse.

[05:40] Gus: Technically, for parity we need: a) same prompt set against OpenAI/TGI and Redwood, b) deterministic sampling settings (temperature/beam/etc), and c) regression eval suite (fuzzy matching + human raters for N=200). We'll propose a scoring rubric.
[05:58] Oliver: For the human raters — we can provide product SMEs to review outputs. We'll likely want an SLA on the pilot window.

[06:12] --- Mid-call: technical deep dive teaser ---
[06:15] Gus: Quick note on private: networking options include VPC peering, customer managed NAT, or on-prem appliance. For on-prem we support KMS integration and air-gapped installs but there are lead times for HSM certs.
[06:32] Samira: HSM integration lead time — can you ballpark?
[06:36] Maya: Typical integration latencies are 4-8 weeks depending on HSM vendor and paperwork. We'll put specifics in the security pack.
[06:48] Priya: How do you handle fallbacks? If dedicated pool overloaded do requests route to hosted? We want graceful degradation.
[06:59] Gus: Yes, smart routing policies exist — can route by latency tier, region, or fall back to smaller cheaper model variant. We'll show a policy example.

[07:15] Oliver: Tokenization again — small differences in UTF normalization lead to token-count deltas across runtimes. Any tooling to normalize?
[07:25] Gus: We have a tokenizer normalization layer in the benchmark harness. It reports token deltas and can re-tokenize to the target model's encoder so metrics are apples-to-apples.

[07:40] --- 10 minute mark: Billing and pricing talk ---
[07:44] Maya: Pricing: hosted is usage-based. Dedicated has reserved capacity contracts. For bench we'll give a short-term hosted pilot price and an estimate for dedicated sizing.
[07:56] Oliver: Is there a minimum commit for Dedicated?
[07:58] Maya: Typically monthly commits for GPUs, but we can scope a short-term trial with pre-paid credits to simulate reserved behavior.

[08:12] Priya: Data retention and logs — can we set retention windows and query audit logs programmatically?
[08:20] Anika: Yes, audit logs are available via our console and can be exported. Retention tiers exist as an add-on.

[08:30] --- misc: deployment questions and edge cases ---
[08:33] Ethan: Any gotchas moving custom LLM adapters or LoRA weights?
[08:38] Gus: We support loading LoRA/inject adapters in both hosted (sandboxed) and private. For hosted, we'd need to validate the artifact. For private, you control everything.

[09:00] Priya: Concerning the vLLM service: our devs rely on some custom wiring in the KV cache for streaming partial outputs — will streaming semantics match?
[09:10] Gus: Streaming is supported. We may need to map how the stream flushes on partial KV evicts; we'll replicate the behavior in the benchmark harness to look for regressions.

[09:25] --- Towards end: timeline and commitments ---
[09:30] Oliver: We're targeting a Q4 pilot decision. The board wants cost/quality numbers by mid-September.
[09:38] Maya: That's doable. We'll deliver the benchmark template within 48 hours and propose the run between 9/7–9/20.
[09:46] Gus: We'll need sample prompts by 9/7 to meet that timeline.
[09:49] Priya: We'll share a 7-day traffic trace and prompt families by 9/7.
[09:55] Samira: Security team will compile SOC2/ISO questions and send them across by Monday.

[10:05] --- Closing recap ---
[10:08] Maya: Recap: Redwood to share benchmark template, security pack, pricing worksheet. Palmetto to share prompts, traffic profile, and compliance questions. SE deep-dive scheduled for 9/10 (tentative). Action items in Fireflies notes.
[10:25] Oliver: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. We'll follow up in email.
[10:35] Maya: Thanks all — we'll send links and next steps.

End of transcript. Note: ASR produced occasional mis-stitched names and tokens (e.g., 'v-l-l-m' sometimes transcribed as 'vll m', 'T G I' or 'T G I'). Human-reviewed action items and next steps above.
